messages:
devops-bot: Scheduled deploy window: 2026-03-20 22:00 UTC -> rolling to prod, target tag v1.8.5. Canary for 15m :ship:
alice.martin: quick context — this is the microfix for tracer leak (no API surface changes). I think this should be a patch by semver, but want ops alignment on tag format and pinning strategy.
ben.kim: agreed patch. question: do we use plain v1.8.5 or annotate hotfix like v1.8.5-hotfix.1? Our release tooling picks up v<semver> tags for changelogs.
carla.ops: tooling caveat: changelog generator ignores +metadata after semver. If we append suffixes we need to update the release-notes script.
dave.wu: my vote: keep semver numeric (v1.8.5) and add annotated lightweight release note entry that says "hotfix: tracer leak". Avoid nonstandard suffixes unless we update tooling.
erin.lopez: +1. Also we should pin the runtime dep in the release for dedicated customers — there was a drift with packer v2.3.0 that triggered the issue. Add a note in the release and pin in the manifest.
alice.martin: action items: (1) ben to create tag v1.8.5 (annotated) and cut release; (2) erin to add pinned dependency and small note in release-notes; (3) carla to verify changelog picks up the annotated tag.
ben.kim: plan: I'll tag from main after CI green. Command: 
```
# create annotated tag
git tag -a v1.8.5 -m "patch: tracer leak fix (release by ops)"
git push origin v1.8.5
```
Will also trigger the release pipeline.
carla.ops: I'll run a quick local dry run of the changelog generator once the tag exists. If it misses, I'll hotfix the script and we can republish the changelog.
dave.wu: rollout policy reminder: canary for 15m, metric checks: error-rate > 1.5% OR latency P95 +30% from baseline => auto-rollback. I put the deploy-bot policy in prod-config.
dave.wu: rollback command (if needed): `/deploy rollback --to v1.8.4 --reason "auto/ops rollback - tracer fix failed"`
erin.lopez: Release notes snippet I'll add: 
"- Fix: memory leak in request tracer causing increased GPU OOMs for long-running streams. No API changes. Recommended: pin packer to v2.3.1 in private manifests."
alice.martin: timing check — can we shift to a quieter window if Canary metrics look risky? We want to avoid peak APAC traffic.
ben.kim: we can bump to 23:30 UTC if needed. For now proceed at 22:00 with canary; ops will monitor.
carla.ops: I'll watch dashboards and add a brief post in #incidents if anything odd within the first 30m.
dave.wu: one more note on semantics: for future microfixes that are pure bugfix/no-api-change, repo policy: semver patch (x.y.z) and do not use suffixes. Use release metadata and changelog to surface hotfix context. Exceptions require ENG-LEADS signoff.
alice.martin: thanks — sounds solid. Ben ping when tag is pushed and I will coordinate the release notes publish.
ben.kim: tag pushed: v1.8.5 -> CI/Release pipeline kicked :rocket:
devops-bot: Deploy started for v1.8.5 on prod (canary instances up).
carla.ops: changelog generator picked up the commit and tag correctly, release-notes draft ready.
erin.lopez: pinned packer 2.3.1 in private manifest and added note.
dave.wu: canary metrics steady at T+10m. No regressions.
alice.martin: moving to full rollout in 5.
ben.kim: full rollout started.
dave.wu: PROD metrics after full rollout: error-rate unchanged, latency nominal. Marking this successful. :tada:
alice.martin: publish release notes and close the change window. Good job team.
carla.ops: leaving a short postmortem note in the release doc about the pinning drift so we remember to add dependency checks to CI.
ben.kim: will update the release tag message with the changelog link.
erin.lopez: nice, thanks everyone.
